Anthony Cirelli (lower body) and Brayden Point (undisclosed) will replace Hagel and Conor Geekie (upper body) in Tuesday's lineup against the Capitals.

items.headline: Hagel scored twice and had an assist in Thursday's 3-1 win over Columbus.
items.text: Hagel extended his goal and point streak to three games and seven points (five goals, two assists); he has 14 shots and a plus-8 rating in that span. Overall, Hagel's 13 goals this season put him sixth overall in the NHL. He has more goals than Auston Matthews (12), Tage Thompson (12), Cole Caufield (12) and Connor McDavid (11). The sniping doesn't seem to be a mirage. Hagel's 17.1 shooting rate is only marginally higher than last season's 16.8; he scored a career-high 36 goals in 2025-26.

items.headline: Hagel scored two goals and added an assist in Wednesday's 8-3 rout of the Sabres.
items.text: After giving Tampa Bay a 3-0 lead early in the second period, Hagel did the rest of his damage in the third, setting up Nikita Kucherov for the first tally in his natural hat trick before potting the final goal of the game himself. It was Hagel's third multi-goal performance of the season, and through 18 games he's delivered 11 goals and 21 points as he looks to reach the 90point mark for the second time in his career.

injuries.longComment: Girgensons exited Tuesday's game against the Capitals late in the first period due to his injury, and it's not yet clear whether he'll be available against Edmonton on Thursday. Max Crozier worked as the fourth-line center during Wednesday's practice session, signaling that the Lightning could elect to dress seven defensemen against the Oilers if Girgensons is unavailable.
injuries.shortComment: Girgensons is considered day-to-day due to an upper-body injury, Lightning reporter Gabby Shirley reports Wednesday.

injuries.longComment: Less than 24 hours after Merzlikins was traded to the Maple Leafs, a timetable for his return to action has been provided. The 32-year-old backstop had an up and down season in 2025-26, where he posted a 14-11-3 record, a 3.39 GAA and an .883 save percentage across 30 regular-season outings. He won't be rushed into action, as the Leafs new goaltender tandem of Sergei Bobrovsky and Anthony Stolarz are still expected to handle the majority of reps between the pipes this upcoming season. However, when Merzlikins is ready to return, he's the clear No. 3 option in Toronto's organization and could still see some playing time at the NHL level if he isn't sent down to AHL Toronto.
injuries.shortComment: Merzlikins is expected to miss 4-6 months to begin the 2026-27 regular season while recovering from a shoulder injury, per Luke Fox of Sportsnet.

It's not yet clear when he'll be able to return to game action, but he'll presumably need to shed his non-contact sweater before he's in consideration to do so. However, Wednesday's activity suggests that he could return around the early estimate of his return timetable.

items.text: Schmaltz is poised to miss his second straight game after being injured in Wednesday's 5-3 loss to Vegas. The Mammoth expect to know more about his timeline soon. Schmaltz has nine goals, 20 points and 48 shots on net in 19 appearances this season.

items.headline: Schmaltz (lower body) is considered a game-time decision for Thursday's matchup against St. Louis, Cole Bagley of KSL Sports reports.
items.text: Schmaltz exited Wednesday's game against the Golden Knights due to his lower-body injury, and it's not yet clear whether he'll be available for the second half of the back-to-back set. If he's unavailable against the Blues, Ben McCartney is a candidate to enter the lineup.

injuries.longComment: The Mammoth indicated Monday that Schmidt was considered out indefinitely, and he was officially placed on injured reserve. It isn't particularly surprising to see him labeled as week-to-week, and it indicates that he's unlikely to return after spending the minimum amount of time on IR. It seems likely that the 35-year-old will be sidelined until at least late November.

injuries.longComment: Demko missed the second half of the 2025-26 season after undergoing hip surgery in January, and he was officially placed on injured reserve last week. He doesn't yet have a clear timetable for when he'll be back in action, but Sedin said that Demko is "taking steps every day" in his recovery process. While Demko is sidelined, Kevin Lankinen and Leevi Merilainen should compete for starts in the Canucks' crease.
injuries.shortComment: Co-president of hockey operations Henrik Sedin said Monday that he hopes Demko (hip) will be ready to return before Christmas, Kevin Woodley of NHL.com reports.

The 34-year-old isn't expected to be in the mix to return to game action until at least January, but he'll likely have the chance to compete for a bottom-six role once he's cleared to suit up.
